newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia oil/gas sector has buoyant yr start.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia oil/gas sector has buoyant yr start.

text.p: Australia's second tier oil and gas sector has started 1997 in a buoyant mood, fired by an exploration success in the offshore Browse Basin that has helped push stocks to new highs.
Many companies have a swag of new drilling planned, but analysts warn more successes may be needed to maintain the sector's momentum.

"Just in the last week or so we are seeing some of the prices come off the top and that reflects that some stocks have just pushed their heads up too far," said Hartley Poynton oil and gas analyst Ann Diamant.
"I think now it's going to come down to exploration success," she said. "If we see exploration successes we will see the sector continue to move on."
Cultus Petroleum NL saw its share price surge from about A$1.45 to a high of A$2.32 on news of a discovery in the Browse Basin offshore Western Australia last month.
Tap Oil NL, Novus Petroleum Ltd, Petroz NL, Oil Search Ltd and Petroleum Securities Australia Ltd have all risen strongly.
The energy index has been a star performer on the Australian stock exchange, rising 49 percent last year, underpinned by strong oil prices, against a 10 percent rise for the overall market.
"It's hard to believe it's really going to continue ... we're in a boom and how long it goes on is hard to guess," said a Melbourne-based oil and gas analyst.
And while the positive tone has been driven by increased exploration, he warned that much of the planned drilling was in second rate territory.
"Money is plentiful ... and that ends up in drilling," he said.
Cultus shares rose sharply when the company said drill reports from the Cornea-1 well pointed to an oil and gas discovery.
Cultus, which has 25 percent of the joint venture, has said previously Cornea could host a potential 100 million barrels of oil.

Interest was boosted by the quality of joint venture partners, Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd, which has 50 percent, and Chevron Corp unit Chevron Asiatic Ltd, with 25 percent.
Analysts said the result lifted other companies across the sector, such as Tap Oil, which is planning to drill a number of wells in the Carnarvon Basin.
"Once one discovery is made, people seem to think other companies are going to make discoveries too," said a second Sydney-based analyst.
However, he said the outlook for the sector remained positive.

Petroleum Securities has announced a series of drill results from the Gulf of Mexico, Oil Search has been boosted by interest in its Moran 1X well in the Papua New Guinea highlands, while Petroz is involved in the Elang and Kakatua development in the Timor Gap.
Many stocks were also underpinned by potential takeover interest and the higher rating afforded the oil gas sector in the U.S. and UK.
"There is still quite a bit of potential for a foreign company to come over here and pick up a Cultus or a Tap Oil," he said.
"Maybe the bubble has burst for a short while. But we see the sector pulling back later in the year and going ahead to outperform the other sectors still," he added.
Diamant said relative to the UK and U.S. Australian stocks still appeared relatively cheap.
"Gas has been the buzzword of late 96 and probably will be in 1997, so companies exposed in Indonesia, the Carnarvon Basin and the Timor Sea will appear attractive," she said.
-- Sydney newsroom 6102 9373-1800
